findings.title: Default upgrade tests never enable rolling-updates
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before the new FeatureSpec block that calls setEnabledFeatures with rolling-updates. The parameterized tests include that null strategy (the default CR path), and the operator guide in this PR states the operator fails unless the preview feature is enabled. Those cases therefore deploy without the feature the rest of the change requires, so testImageChange(null) and testCacheMaxCount(null) exercise a configuration the operator is documented to reject. The enablement also uses setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)), which replaces any features already on the CR instead of adding rolling-updates, so a non-null strategy run can drop other enabled features the test deployment depended on.

findings.title: Documented compatibility commands hardcode --features and can override real config
findings.body: The update-compatibility doc macro always appends --features=rolling-updates after the caller's parameters. The same guide warns that every option from the running deployment must be passed or the metadata and check result are wrong. Keycloak treats --features as a single list option, so a later --features=rolling-updates replaces an earlier --features=... from ${parameters} rather than adding the preview flag. Users following the documented command can therefore snapshot or check a different feature set than production, and the tool will report rolling vs recreate based on that altered config.
